title: Choose the visual world for Grocy Next
question: The roll assigned Enamel Canisters. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Enamel Canisters
options.lineage: European enamelware kitchen canisters (Zucker, Mehl, Kaffee)
options.thesis: The pantry as a shelf of labelled canisters: every product shows how full it is.
materials: cobalt rim as the shell colour
options.viewport: Cobalt rail left; Today board: Use first / Running low / Due this week / Agent proposals; each stock row carries a canister fill gauge with a minimum tick.
options.risk: Gauges need a sane scale; products with no minimum get an honest amount-only state, not a fake fill.

raised.raise: Length is exact time: due bars on the Today board measure the real days left, on one 14-day scale.
Amounts set right-aligned in tabular figures, tight to the column edge, unit beside the number.
Nothing labelled twice: no stat tiles that repeat a table; counts live on the filter that shows them.
Data at full contrast; grey only for labels, never for amounts or dates.
Each domain (Stock, Shopping, Chores, Agent) keeps one fixed marker colour across nav and board.
Every product keeps fixed furniture in fixed places: name, amount, gauge, date, actions.

options.label: Nutrition Facts Panel
options.thesis: The household read like a facts panel: heavy rules, black grotesk, numbers that cannot lie.
options.viewport: Top bar; Today board set as one 'Household Facts' panel with thick-thin rule sections, stock below as a ruled list.
options.risk: Familiar: the label cliché many food apps reach for; monochrome may feel austere on a phone.

options.label: Factory Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Every product as a numbered catalog entry.
options.viewport: Black index of product numbers, colour codes in place of names.
options.case: Fuses poorly: replacing names with codes breaks a kitchen task.
options.risk: Unreadable at a glance on a phone.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.thesis: Lists as tracklists with exact running totals.
options.viewport: Shopping list as side A / side B.
options.case: Fuses poorly: handwriting is playful and unlike Grocy.
options.kept: Right-aligned tabular amounts tight to the edge.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.thesis: Time flows upward; length is exact duration.
options.viewport: Due items as a vertical score.
options.case: Fuses poorly: notation is foreign to the audience.
options.kept: Bar length equals exact days left.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Products as a ranked mascot roster.
options.viewport: Pastel product grid with name plates.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the user ruled out playful.

options.label: Midnight Transit Diagram
options.viewport: Dark map of chores and stock as routes.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a pantry is not a network; clarity drops.
options.risk: Map metaphor hides the list task.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: The household as a pure black-and-white data field.
options.case: Fuses poorly: strobing art is not a kitchen tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard (Grocy-style)
canonCard.thesis: Grocy's own layout, executed impeccably: dark sidebar, dense tables, blue primary.
canonCard.viewport: Dark left sidebar, stock overview table with due badges, toolbar on top.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every self-hosted admin panel by design.
